note:
One override, for debt. Lennar's total debt row carried four of fifteen years and no quarters at all, and the gap is structural rather than a missing tag: the whole of its borrowing is one balance-sheet line, 'Senior notes and other debts payable, net', tagged us-gaap:LongTermDebt -- but Lennar prints that line once per segment column, and companyfacts keeps only the undimensioned fact. Of its recent filings only the FY2019/FY2020 and FY2025 10-Ks tag a consolidated figure outside the segment axis; those are exactly the years that resolved ($9,573.7M, $7,421.6M, $5,875.0M, and FY2024's $4,189.2M from the FY2025 10-K's comparative column), and each one is correct -- FY2025's $5,875.0M is Homebuilding $4,084.7M plus Financial Services $1,790.3M. Everything else was blank.

The 10-Qs do report a consolidated total, as the srt:ConsolidationItemsAxis 'Operating Segments' column: $5,256.5M at Q1 FY2026 and $6,011.2M at Q2, the latter reconciling to Homebuilding $4,047.5M + Financial Services $1,963.7M + Multifamily and Lennar Other at zero. That column is a dimensional fact, so companyfacts does not carry it and only the filed statements can supply it. Hence the two candidates below: the undimensioned consolidated line where Lennar tags one, else the operating-segment total. First-match-wins means the 10-K's own consolidated figure always outranks the segment roll-up, and the roll-up is only reached where no consolidated line exists.

No 'from'/'to' bound is wanted here, which also keeps this binding clear of the fiscal-vs-calendar hazard CarMart's carries: resolve() keys annual years by fiscal year and resolve_quarters() by the calendar year of the period end, and for Lennar's November year-end a year boundary would read differently on the two paths. Both candidates name a specific column of a specific statement, so a year either has that column or has nothing -- there is no partial total to guard against.

What this binding deliberately does NOT do is fill the remaining gaps from the segment columns. FY2021 through FY2024 and Q3 FY2026 print a Homebuilding debt line and no Financial Services one -- $4,652.3M, $4,047.3M, $2,816.5M, $2,258.3M and $4,297.3M respectively -- so the consolidated total for those periods is not on the face of any balance sheet, only in the notes, which build_factbase does not read (it takes FilingSummary's 'Statements' category alone). Binding Homebuilding alone would present a segment column as the company's total debt, understating FY2023 by the ~$1.5B of Financial Services warehouse borrowing it carries. Those periods stay blank, which is the honest reading of what was filed.

metrics.label: Senior notes and other debts payable, net
metrics.note: Lennar's entire borrowing is this one line; it files an unclassified balance sheet with no current portion split out, so total debt is this row alone and current_debt is legitimately absent rather than missing. The first candidate is the consolidated line as tagged in the FY2019, FY2020 and FY2025 10-Ks. The second is the 10-Qs' 'Operating Segments' total under srt:ConsolidationItemsAxis -- the consolidated column of a statement that tags no undimensioned figure -- and NOT a single segment: the segment members sit under us-gaap:StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis and render as 'Homebuilding', 'Lennar Financial Services', 'Operating Segments | Homebuilding' and so on, none of which this matches.
